title: "Materials"

<p class="page-intro">Guides, documentation, and teaching notes. These currently cover <a href="https://cran.r-project.org/web/packages/phdid/index.html" target="_blank">phdid</a>, my R package for partial homogeneity in staggered difference-in-differences. I will be adding notes on economics studies and coding here as I go.</p>

<div class="research-section-title">
<h2>phdid Vignettes</h2>
</div>
<hr class="section-divider">
<p class="section-note">Written to walk someone through empirical applications of the package in R.</p>
<div class="materials-grid">
<div class="writing-card">
<p class="writing-date">phdid vignette</p>
<p class="writing-title"><a class="stretched-link" href="https://cran.r-project.org/web/packages/phdid/vignettes/mpdta.html" target="_blank">Minimum Wages and Teen Employment: Recovering Partial Homogeneity</a></p>
<p class="writing-desc">Walks through the county-level minimum wage analysis of Callaway and Sant'Anna (2021): taking cohort-time effects from <code>did::att_gt()</code>, testing whether there is heterogeneity worth recovering, and grouping the effects with both a point partition and a Dirichlet Process posterior.</p>
<span class="writing-link">Read the vignette <i class="bi bi-arrow-right-short"></i></span>
</div>
<div class="writing-card">
<p class="writing-date">phdid vignette</p>
<p class="writing-title"><a class="stretched-link" href="https://cran.r-project.org/web/packages/phdid/vignettes/simulation.html" target="_blank">When Partial Homogeneity Helps, and When It Does Not</a></p>
<p class="writing-desc">A reduced-scale Monte Carlo showing how the precision gains from pooling cohort-time effects depend on how well separated those effects are, and how the estimators compare on variance, bias, and interval coverage.</p>
<span class="writing-link">Read the vignette <i class="bi bi-arrow-right-short"></i></span>
</div>
</div>
